maria: Heads-up — I ran a continuous-batching sweep on the new heuristic (cohort-based slice + queue-priority) and we need to decide final max_tokens_per_batch targets per cardset. Quick summary below and a proposal.

maria: TL;DR: H100/A100 need much higher token ceilings than A10/L4/T4 to avoid underpacking; but kernel fallbacks create p99 cliffs if we push too far on mixed workloads. Thoughts?

kevin: nice. can you paste the raw numbers? :eyes:

maria: paste below (perf-bot produced these):

perf-bot: run 2026-03-10T14:05Z — continuous-batching/sweep#42
perf-bot: config: cohort_slice=dynamic; priority_queue=entropy-weighted; kv_cache_prefetch=on

maria: ```
GPU   | max_tokens_batch(prev) | max_tokens_batch(proposed) | avg_throughput_tok/s | p99_latency_ms | notes
H100  | 180k                   | 420k                       | 1.8M                 | 55             | +8% throughput, p99 stable
A100  | 160k                   | 320k                       | 1.2M                 | 62             | +6% throughput, small p99 bump
A10   | 110k                   | 150k                       | 480k                 | 75             | +3% throughput, kernel fallback risk
L4    | 90k                    | 130k                       | 350k                 | 120            | +1% throughput, p99 regress on sparse KV
T4    | 80k                    | 110k                       | 300k                 | 140            | no throughput win, p99 regressed
```

maria: notes: throughput measured across mixed prompt distro (20% long, 60% medium, 20% short). KV cache fragmentation looked higher on L4/T4 — see below.

sophia: can you show kernel selector logs and kv frag numbers? my worry is small-card kernels mis-ejecting and causing extra mem copies.

maria: attached selector dump (summarized):

maria: ```
H100: kernel=compiled_fast_attn_v3 (90%), fallback=none
A100: kernel=fast_attn_opt (75%), fallback=small_matmul (25%)
A10: kernel=fast_attn_opt (60%), fallback=small_matmul (40%)
L4: kernel=small_matmul (80%), fallback=scalar_attention (20%)
T4: kernel=small_matmul (85%), fallback=scalar_attention (15%)
```

maria: KV fragmentation (percent of requests seeing >2 fragments): H100 6%, A100 10%, A10 28%, L4 34%, T4 36%.

kevin: those kv numbers explain the p99. for L4/T4, when we push token ceilings they create longer sequences per batch which fragments the KV cache more often -> causes additional memcpy and kernel fallback.

oleg: agree. proposal: keep higher ceilings for H100/A100 as-is, but add a soft ceiling + fallback gating for A10/L4/T4. e.g.

oleg: ```json
{"max_tokens_per_batch":{"H100":"420000","A100":"320000","A10":"150000_soft","L4":"120000_soft","T4":"110000_soft"},"soft_ceiling_behavior":"prefer_smaller_slices_when_kv_frag>20%","soft_ceiling_window_ms":50}
```

ricardo: how would the gating work at runtime? do we monitor per-device kv_frag over short windows and dynamically clamp?

oleg: yes — runtime maintains per-cardlet sliding counter for kv_frag and kernel_fallback events over 10s window. if kv_frag>threshold, cohort slice size reduces by 15% and we target kernels with smaller working set.

sophia: love the approach. one ask: add a canary rollout with traffic shaping by prompt entropy cohorts. we should test mixed traffic with 30% high-entropy prompts to stress fragmentation.

maria: agreed. I ran a quick canary: 5% traffic for 6h on A10 pool with soft ceilings enabled. result: p99 decreased 12% vs full-proposed, but throughput dropped 2%.

kevin: that's an acceptable trade for A10. For L4/T4 maybe we need to increase prefetch aggressiveness instead of shrinking slices — could reduce kv frag.

maria: tried that too: kv_prefetch++ reduced frag by ~6pp on L4 but added CPU overhead and slightly higher scheduling jitter. tradeoffs.

perf-bot: benchmark note: prefetch_on + soft_ceiling for L4/T4 gives best p99 with only -1.5% throughput vs proposed defaults.

ricardo: rollout plan idea:
- step 0: ship config as oleg pasted for soft ceilings
- step 1: canary 5% per cardset for 24h with perf monitoring + kernel_fallback alerting
- step 2: if p99 improves or stable and throughput loss <3% promote to 30%
- step 3: full roll after 72h safe window

maria: I'll draft the service-config PR and the SLO check playbook. Also adding a per-model opt-out flag for customers sensitive to any throughput reduction.

sophia: one more: add a kernel-selector telemetry tag so we can correlate kernel switch events with user queries (anonymized). makes debugging regressions faster.

maria: good call. I'll include that in the PR.

kevin: looks solid. :thumbsup:

oleg: ping @maria when PR is up, I'll own rollout automation.

maria: will do. thanks all. closing the loop here — I'll post the PR link and perf dashboards once ready. :rocket:

perf-bot: automated reminder: export sweep artifacts to /benchmarks/continuous-batching/2026-03-10/sweep42.zip

maria: exported. link: https://internal.redwood/benchmarks/continuous-batching/2026-03-10/sweep42.zip
